description: Find the best EV charge points along a route, with the REAL extra travel time of stopping at each one — never a straight-line guess. Provide `origin` + `destination` (a route is computed) or an existing route's `geometry_polyline6`, plus optional `connectors` ("ccs", "type2", "chademo", "type1", "tesla", "domestic", "other"), `min_kw` (e.g. 50 for rapid only), `available_only` and `max_detour_minutes` (default 10). Charge points come from operator-published feeds, are costed through the routing engine with your costing (a `truck` profile makes detours respect dimensional/ADR restrictions) and ranked most powerful first, since minutes off the clock are bought with kilowatts. Each result carries max_power_kw, connector_standards, best_connector, evse_count, detour_minutes/detour_km and, where a live feed backs it, available_now. IMPORTANT: there is no national charge-point registry — every deployment covers only the operators it has onboarded, so ALWAYS show the returned `coverage_note` alongside the results. An empty `results` means "none from these operators within the detour budget", NEVER "there are no chargers here". Statuses are live only when availability_live is true; otherwise they are the values captured at the last ingest and must not be described as current. `say` is ALWAYS present and is the whole answer as one short spoken line, composed by the gateway with the coverage already inside the claim rather than appended to it: it scopes its superlative to the operators this deployment holds, and an empty result's line says the emptiness is about those operators. Prefer reading it verbatim to writing your own summary. Requires the MapMap gateway; answers a clear error when the deployment has no charge-point dataset. Display the returned charging_attribution with the results.

CostingKind.description:
Costing models exposed by the MCP tools (a deliberate subset of the
Valhalla costing list), serialised in snake_case exactly as Valhalla
names them.

oneOf.description:
Truck costing; honours dimensional limits and, when a `truck`
profile is supplied, ADR dangerous-goods restrictions.
Bicycle costing; tune it with a `bicycle` options object.

Pedestrian (walking) costing; tune it with a `pedestrian` options
object (lit streets, wheelchair/blind, hiking difficulty).

Motor scooter (moped) costing: like auto but prefers lower-speed
roads and may use ways closed to larger motor vehicles.

LatLon.description: A WGS84 coordinate in decimal degrees: a {lat, lon} object (preferred), or a GeoJSON [lon, lat] array with LONGITUDE FIRST, the same order as every polygon field on this server.

TruckSpec.description:
Truck profile for routing: physical dimensions plus the ADR
dangerous-goods declaration. Omitted dimensions default to the EU
maximum authorised dimensions of Council Directive 96/53/EC (4.0 m
height, 2.55 m width, 16.5 m length, 40 t gross weight).

gross_weight_t.description: Gross combination weight in metric tonnes.

hazmat.description:
Whether the vehicle carries dangerous goods (ADR). Defaults to
false.

tunnel_code.description:
ADR 8.6.4 tunnel restriction code of the load, e.g. "B", "C5000D",
"B/D", or "(—)"/"none" for explicitly unrestricted. Leave unset if
unknown: a hazmat load without a code is conservatively treated as
code B (allowed only through category-A tunnels).

available_only.description:
Keep only charge points with a bay reported free right now. Needs
the deployment to have a live availability feed; without one the
call is refused rather than silently returning nothing.

connectors.description:
Keep only charge points offering at least one of these connector
standards: "type2", "type1", "ccs", "chademo", "tesla", "domestic"
or "other". Omitted ⇒ every standard.

costing.description:
Costing model for the route and detour matrix: "auto" (default),
"truck", "bicycle", "pedestrian" or "motor_scooter".

geometry_polyline6.description:
An existing route geometry as an encoded polyline6 (the `route`
tool's `geometry_polyline6`). Provide either this or `origin` +
`destination`, not both.

max_detour_minutes.description: Largest acceptable detour in minutes (default 10, at most 120).

min_kw.description:
Keep only charge points whose best connector is rated at least this
many kW (e.g. 50 for rapid charging only).

origin.description: Route origin (with `destination`, when no geometry is given).

truck.description:
Truck profile (dimensions + ADR declaration). Requires costing
"truck"; the detours then respect dimensional/ADR restrictions.

name: cheapest_charging_along_route

ChargerConnector.description: The highest-rated connector at a charge point.

dc.description: Whether this connector delivers DC (rapid) rather than AC.

power_kw.description: Rated power in kW, where the operator publishes enough to know it.

power_kw_source.description:
"declared" when the operator published the rating, "derived" when
it was computed from voltage × amperage × phases. Never present
the two as the same thing to a user.

ChargerHit.description: One charge point along the route, with its real engine-computed detour.

along_route_position.description: How far along the route the charge point sits, 0.0–1.0.

available_now.description:
Whether a bay is free right now. Present only where a live
availability feed backs the claim — absent means unknown, never
"occupied".

best_connector.description: The highest-rated connector at the site.

connector_standards.description: Every distinct connector standard at the site.

detour_km.description:
Extra distance of the detour in kilometres, when the engine
reported distances.

detour_minutes.description: Real extra travel time of stopping here, minutes.

evse_count.description: Number of charging positions (EVSEs) at the site.

max_power_kw.description: Highest rated power at the site, kW.

name.description: Site name, where the operator publishes one.

off_route_m.description: Straight-line offset from the route geometry, metres.

source.description: Which operator feed this came from.

status_live.description:
Whether the status came from a live feed rather than the last
ingest.

updated_at.description: When the operator last updated this record.

ChargingSource.description: One operator's coverage and licence, as published by the deployment.

chargers.description: How many charge points this operator contributes.

coverage_note.description:
Plain-language statement of what this operator's feed does and
does not cover.

licence.description: Licence or statutory basis of the feed.

availability_live.description:
Whether statuses are live (a bring-your-own availability feed) or
the values captured at the last ingest.

availability_note.description: Plain-language explanation of what the statuses mean here.

candidate_cap.description: The matrix fan-out cap in force.

candidates_considered.description:
Charge points matching the filters that passed the corridor
pre-filter.

candidates_costed.description:
Candidates actually costed through the engine (fan-out capped at
`candidate_cap`, most powerful kept).

charging_attribution.description:
Attribution string for the charge-point operators actually
returned — display it with the results (a licence obligation).

costing.description: The costing the detours were computed with.

coverage_note.description:
**Always present.** What this deployment's charge-point dataset
does and does not cover. An empty `results` means "none from these
operators within the budget" — never "there are no chargers here".
Show this to the user alongside the results.

note.description: Why `results` is empty, when it is — the cause, not a bare list.

results.description:
Charge points within the detour budget, most powerful first
(power, then detour).

route_duration_s.description:
Direct origin→destination travel time in seconds (same estimator
as the detour legs), when routable.

route_length_m.description: Length of the route geometry in metres.

say.description:
**Always present.** The whole answer as one short spoken line,
composed by the gateway. Coverage is inside the claim rather than
appended to it: the line scopes its superlative to the operators
this deployment holds, and an empty result's line says the
emptiness is about those operators, never about the road. Safe to
read to a driver verbatim.

sources.description:
Every operator in the dataset, with its own coverage note and
licence. Present even when `results` is empty.
